Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

hexamap 0.9.0

Release candidate for the first CRAN release.

  • Spelling checked (inst/WORDLIST, Language: en-US) with a spelling test.
  • New visual regression tests with ‘vdiffr’ for base and ggplot2 output.
  • Test coverage is 98.9%.
  • Smaller vignette figures, to keep the installed package small.
  • Added cran-comments.md.

hexamap 0.8.1

Documentation

  • New vignettes:
    • vignette("hexamap"): getting started (data, isolines, colors, missing cells, layouts, Lexis diagrams, ggplot2, saving figures).
    • vignette("apc-patterns"): age, period and cohort effects alone, in pairs and all together, on Lexis diagrams and hexamaps, and the identification problem.
    • vignette("overdose"): Figure 1C/D of Jalal and Burke (2020), the 1975 cohort comparison, rate ratios and quantile scales.
  • The hex sticker labels its three isolines A, P and C.

hexamap 0.8.0

Documentation

  • New README with the motivation for hexamaps, a Lexis-vs-hexamap comparison, the overdose example and a ggplot2 example.
  • New hex sticker (man/figures/logo.png), drawn with hexamap itself by data-raw/hexsticker.R.
  • citation("hexamap") gives the Epidemiology letter and the package.
  • New pkgdown site configuration and GitHub Actions workflow.

hexamap 0.7.0

New data

  • New datasets overdose_white_men (age-by-year matrix of rates) and overdose_white_men_long (one row per age and year, with deaths, population and a reliability flag): accidental drug overdose deaths among white men in the United States, ages 15-70, 1999-2018, from CDC WONDER. These are the data of Figure 1C/D in Jalal and Burke (2020). Following the CDC WONDER data use restrictions, counts of 9 or fewer deaths and the rates based on them are not included.

hexamap 0.6.0

New features

  • New gg_hexamap() draws hexamaps and Lexis diagrams with ‘ggplot2’ (in Suggests). It returns a ggplot object that can be modified with labs(), theme() and other ggplot2 functions. A named list of matrices gives one panel per element, with a shared color scale.
  • New autoplot() method for hexamap_layout objects.
  • hexamap_layout() cells gain a fraction column with each value’s position along the color scale.

hexamap 0.5.0

New features

  • New lexis_map() draws a traditional Lexis diagram (square tiles, periods on the x axis, ages on the y axis, cohorts on the diagonals) with all the options of hexamap(), for side-by-side comparisons. hexamap_layout() and hexamap() gain a tiles argument, and apc_to_xy() accepts tiles = "square".
  • New simulate_apc() generates rates from a log-linear age-period-cohort model, with effects given as functions or vectors and optional Poisson noise.
  • New as_apc_matrix() reshapes long data (one row per age-period combination, e.g. from CDC WONDER) into an age-by-period matrix on a regular grid, with NA for missing combinations.
  • New apc_rates() computes rates from counts and population, with NA where the population is zero or missing.

Changes

  • The hexagon element of hexamap_layout objects is now called tile. A new tiles element records the tile shape.

hexamap 0.4.0

New features

  • New highlight argument draws chosen ages, periods and/or cohorts as highlighted lines with bold labels, e.g. highlight = list(cohort = 1975). The values need not be isolines. col and lwd set the line color and width.
  • New labels argument sets the prefixes of the isoline labels, e.g. labels = c(age = "Age ", period = ""). Names left out keep the defaults "A: ", "P: " and "C: ".
  • New isolines argument chooses which isolines to draw.
  • New title_adj argument aligns the title and subtitle.

Changes

  • Isolines now fall on round values by default. isoline_interval is the smallest round spacing (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, …) that is a multiple of interval and gives at most 8 isolines. The first isolines are the first ages and periods that are multiples of it. For the paper’s example (ages 15-70, 1999-2018), the defaults now match the published figure: A: 20-70, P: 2000 and 2010, C: 1930-2000.
  • label_size defaults to 0.7 (was 0.5).

hexamap 0.3.0

New features

  • New hexamap_palette() returns colors from the “jet” palette of Jalal and Burke (2020) or from any grDevices::hcl.pals() palette. Use it via the new palette and n_colors arguments of hexamap().
  • New midpoint argument for diverging scales, such as rate ratios on a log scale (midpoint = 1) or differences (midpoint = 0). The color limits are made symmetric around the midpoint, and the default palette becomes the diverging “Blue-Red 3”.
  • Missing cells are drawn in na_color (default light grey), with a “Missing” key below the colorbar (na_label). Use na_color = NA to leave them blank, as before.
  • New hex_border and hex_border_width arguments.

Changes

  • The default palette remains the paper’s “jet”, now generated by hexamap_palette(). palette = "viridis" is a perceptually uniform alternative that is readable by people with color vision deficiencies.
  • Hexagon borders are drawn in each hexagon’s own color by default (hex_border = "fill"), which removes the thin white seams that many PDF and PNG viewers show between tiles.
  • Colorbar ticks are now round values within the limits (and the midpoint, if any) on linear and log scales, and every 20th percentile on quantile scales.

hexamap 0.2.0

New features

  • New hexamap_layout() computes a hexamap without drawing it: hexagon centers and colors, isolines, color scale and colorbar ticks. Draw it with plot() or use it to build custom graphics. hexamap() now returns this layout invisibly. Layouts print a short summary.
  • New apc_to_xy() converts ages and periods to hexamap coordinates, to add points, lines or text to a hexamap.
  • first_age, first_period and interval default to the numeric row (age) and column (period) names of data. Age or period names that are unequally spaced, or whose spacing differs from each other, give an error.
  • New legend argument turns the colorbar off.

Changes

  • The hexamap, its labels and the colorbar are now sized to fit the current plotting region on any device, so hexamaps can be combined with par(mfrow = ). Titles are drawn in the top margin and no longer overlap the period labels.
  • colorbar_width is now the width of the colorbar in inches (default 0.15). colorbar_height is its height as a fraction of the hexamap height (default 0.5).
  • zoom_factor is deprecated and ignored.
  • title_text and subtitle_text default to no title. The subtitle is no longer passed through prettyNum(), which added thousands separators to years (“1,999”).
  • Hexagons are drawn with a single polygon() call and isolines with segments(), which is faster and gives smaller files.

hexamap 0.1.2

Bug fixes

  • The colorbar no longer draws shifted, overlapping color blocks (2:ncol+1 was evaluated as 3:(ncol+1)).
  • Every palette color can now appear on the hexagons. Previously the top color was never used because ncol breaks gave only ncol - 1 bins.
  • NA cells are skipped instead of making the default color range fail with “‘from’ must be a finite number”. Data with no finite values give a clear error.
  • The log color scale no longer fails on zeros: values <= 0 are drawn in the lowest color, with a warning. A non-positive colorbar_range with a log scale gives an error.
  • colorbar_scale accepts "linear", "log" and "quantile" (and the legacy names "Normal", "Log", "Percentile") in any letter case. Unknown names give a clear error instead of “object ‘data_cutpoints’ not found”.
  • Colorbar tick labels are correct for palettes of any length (they assumed 100 colors). They now show 3 significant digits, so small rates are no longer rounded to 0.
  • Percentile ticks are only drawn for the quantile scale.
  • hexamap() restores the graphical parameters it changes.
  • An empty subtitle_text is no longer drawn as “NA”.
  • scale_units is now displayed above the colorbar, as documented.
  • Inputs are validated with informative errors. Data frames of numeric columns are accepted.

hexamap 0.1.1

  • Added GitHub Actions R CMD check on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu (R release, devel and oldrel-1).

hexamap 0.1.0

  • Initial package skeleton. hexamap() is the general version of the function from the original scripts; the figure-specific variant (hexagon_apc_functions.R) was removed.
  • Added create_hexamap(), a wrapper that keeps the code from the Epidemiology (2020) eAppendix working.
